status_summary: National Security Presidential Memorandum 2 (signed 2025-02-04) directed Treasury, State, Justice and Commerce to enforce Iran sanctions and export controls, including a campaign to drive Iran's oil exports to zero, and directed the US Ambassador to the UN to work with allies to complete the snapback of UN sanctions; a law-firm analysis reports UN sanctions were reinstated on 2025-09-28. NPR reports that the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February 2026. A US-Iran memorandum of understanding dated 2026-06-17 (the Islamabad memorandum) provided, according to its posted text, that the US would lift its naval blockade, issue Treasury waivers for Iranian oil exports, make frozen funds usable and impose no new sanctions while a final deal was negotiated, with sanctions ending on an agreed schedule under that deal. Al Jazeera reports that President Trump declared the memorandum ended on 2026-07-07 and that it expired in mid-August, and the Washington Examiner reports he announced a restart of the blockade on 2026-07-13; the sources found do not show whether the oil waivers were issued. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced an expanded sanctions campaign called Operation Economic Outcast on 2026-08-24, and Treasury issued further actions under it on 2026-10-01 against Iran's automotive, rail, manufacturing and metals sectors, with a warning of possible secondary sanctions on foreign financial institutions; the release states that Iran's oil revenues have fallen to zero as the US maritime blockade takes hold (Treasury's characterization). US and Iranian officials held direct talks on 2026-09-22 at the UN General Assembly, the first reported direct contact since June, and press reports say President Trump announced another meeting; Iran's stated conditions included lifting the blockade and releasing frozen assets. Public Law 119-111, enacted 2026-09-18, extended the Iran Sanctions Act's expiration from 2026 to 2031. As of 2026-10-01 the sanctions track follows the Mandate's call to reinstate and expand sanctions, but the June 2026 memorandum committed the US to end sanctions in exchange for a final deal, which differs from the Mandate; whether Iran has been denied nuclear capability was not established by the sources found.

timeline.event: NSPM-2 directs Treasury to enforce Iran sanctions and roll back relief, State and Treasury to drive Iranian oil exports to zero including those to China, Justice to pursue sanctions-evasion networks, and the UN Ambassador to work with allies to complete the UN snapback.

UN sanctions on Iran are reinstated through the snapback process, according to a DLA Piper analysis, which lists asset freezes and travel bans on 121 individuals and entities and restrictions on enrichment, missiles, arms and shipping.

Month-level date: NPR, republished by Michigan Public on 2026-08-24, reports that the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February 2026 and describes a monthslong US naval blockade that has cut off most goods to Iran; it gives no start date for the blockade.

The US and Iran sign the Islamabad memorandum of understanding, per Wikipedia and Al Jazeera. Its posted text commits the US to oil export waivers, usable frozen funds, no new sanctions during talks and a phased end to the naval blockade, with sanctions ending on an agreed schedule under a final deal.
Al Jazeera reports that President Trump declared the memorandum ended and both sides suspended their commitments after clashes over Strait of Hormuz shipping in late June.
President Trump announces that the US military will restart its blockade of Iranian ports, according to the Washington Examiner.

Treasury Secretary Bessent announces Operation Economic Outcast. Axios reports about 60 entities, individuals and vessels sanctioned, several licenses suspended, expansion into digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping, and a plan to give countries timelines to end Iran-related business or face secondary sanctions.

Public Law 119-111 (Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026) is enacted. Its only Iran provision, Section 201, changes the expiration year in section 13(b) of the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 from 2026 to 2031.

US special envoy Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi hold about three hours of talks at the UN General Assembly, the first direct contact reported since June; Iran's stated conditions include lifting the blockade and releasing frozen assets, and President Trump says another meeting will follow.

Treasury announces further Operation Economic Outcast actions: two OFAC sectoral determinations (automotive and rail) under Executive Order 13902 and designations covering Iranian car makers, a railway company, a heavy-equipment maker and a steel and oil export network, with a warning to foreign financial institutions about secondary sanctions. The release ties the action to the US maritime blockade.

title: Reinstate and expand Iran sanctions and deny Iran nuclear capability
uncertainties: The 2026 war, blockade and sanctions-campaign context rests on press reports (Michigan Public, Axios, Al Jazeera, Washington Examiner) and Treasury releases; the war start month and blockade timing were given only at month level in the original sources. The memorandum text is from Iran Watch (a non-government site) and its signing date comes from Wikipedia and Al Jazeera; whether Treasury issued any oil waivers during June to July 2026 was not established, and the Wikipedia article's latest entries are from mid-June. Why the blockade was described as ongoing before the 2026-07-13 restart announcement was not resolved. The DLA Piper article is dated only to October 2025 on its URL (2025-10-01 used as a month-level date). The Federal Register query for Maximum Pressure and Iran since 2025-01-20 returned no documents, so no rule or executive order beyond NSPM-2 was identified for 2025. Public diplomacy, regional security assistance and Israel-related Mandate elements were not researched, and a final nuclear outcome was not found. Reports differ on where the June memorandum was agreed (the posted text is titled for Islamabad; LIGA.net places the meeting in Switzerland), which does not affect its terms. The outcome of the 2026-09-22 talks and any follow-up meeting were not found.
